problems.problem: The rendered poster (first image) still shows the same grotesque sans letterforms for TOM FORD / TOBACCO VANILLE / EAU DE PARFUM — the geometry font paths are unchanged to arial.ttf. This is a neutral system font with no luxury character, unlike the crafted serif/gold logotype of the Armani Privé reference. The right column also keeps an uneven rhythm: logo ends at y245, title starts y310, but the subtitle sits far below at y420, leaving a loose 85px gap that reads as placeholder spacing rather than a designed block.

Bottle height ratio 0.5903 is within the 0.50–0.65 hero band and bottom edge (1245 = 86.5% of 1440) respects margins, so scale is correct. However the lower right two-thirds of the wine-red field remains empty; decoration.enabled is still false, so the reserved gold accent slot never anchors the text column to the product zone. Balance leans entirely on the lower-right amber pool of light, which is atmospheric but not a compositional device.

The wine-red cyclorama, diagonal wall shadow and warm amber glow are internally coherent, but the concept is still a generic dramatic backdrop: no material cue (tobacco leaf, lacquer, wood, vanilla pod) expresses Tobacco Vanille, trailing the fig slice, red lacquer splash and sandalwood plank that give the three references their narrative identity.

Against the references the residual gap is typographic (Arial vs. a designed logotype) and conceptual (empty seamless wall vs. sculptural prop interplay). Lighting quality, palette harmony and grounding are now close to reference level; the result is a polished draft, not yet a fully resolved campaign.
